body:

[DarnyBoy1982] It likely due to shipping restrictions on lithium batteries, pretty sure they will be via shipping container only.
[DraggyX] I didnt know that you can use multi coupons at once
[Clear] Always been able to stack seller and AliExpress codes.
[homersyd] can you bring the 200W 27000mAh CCC power bank onto the plane?
[silverham] 20,000mAh Product page says:
Battery Capacity 5000mAh (14.8V/74Wh) (5000*4)
So internal voltage is 3.7V (14.8V / 4). Therefore 3.7V * 20000mAh / 1000 = 74Wh
For the 27,000mAh one, i checked the manufacturer website:
https://ventiontech.com/products/27000mah-power-bank-1
Battery Capacity: 4500mAh (22.2V/99.9Wh) (4500*6)
So internal voltage is 3.7V (22.2V / 6). Therefore 3.7V * 27000mAh / 1000 = 99.9Wh
Airline approval only required if ≥ 100Wh. So yes can take on a plane, though personally i would only get the 99.9Wh one if CCC mark otherwise it is uncomfortably close to the threshold for my liking.
[sachk] weighs about 640g apparently, listing doesn't actually say anywhere even in the spec sheet in the final image in the description. quite heavy but if you actually need charging output this high then it's a fantastic price.
[GalaxySkater58] I just weighed mine out of pure curiosity after reading this. 440g.
It's really quite a good power bank. Very premium and great output
[Kegsta] Your this one last time. Haven't used it much but it's very impressive.
[mynameisborat] Bought a Venition 140W battery pack, and it's honestly one of the shoddiest products I've ever purchased.
The battery doesn't hold its charge for more than a few days. And once it's completely drained, it takes an absurdly long time to recharge potentially an entire day! This started happening when the battery pack wasn't even a month old.
Absolutely pathetic quality.
Do yourself a favour and get an Anker instead. I'd also recommend buying from a local retailer so you have an easier time dealing with warranty claims if something goes wrong.
